title: Atlas facility event record
description: One dated event in the life of a facility (S09; D-083, proposed: H-2 'Minimal event schema (Recommended)'). The records live in data/events.json (canonical) and data/staging/events.json (staging). This file is the one home of the event shape and of the event-type vocabulary. Why each type exists, how a plan differs from an occurrence, the ID rule and how a facility's status is derived from events are in docs/architecture/facility-dataset.md. There is deliberately no status, no planned date and no owner or operator field: status is derived from events by tools/facility_status.py and never stored (MA §5.6, R-8); a planned date lives only in the ATTRIBUTION claim that states the plan (ER-8); ownership and operation are S10 edges (R-5). An event is never an edge endpoint (relationship-taxonomy.md §10).

id.description: event-, the subject's ID without its type prefix, the event type, and the date with its own precision (facility-dataset.md §6, EI-1).

subject.description: What the event happened to. An occurrence (opened, expanded, closed) always has a facility as its subject. An announced event has the facility when the plan concerns an existing facility record, and otherwise the announcing company, because a site known only from a plan gets no facility record (ER-8; S09 Part B §16).

date.description: The date of the event at the precision the source gives (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD). For announced, the date of the announcement, never the date the plan names.

claim_ids.description: The claims that state the event. An occurrence rests on at least one FACT or DERIVATION; an announced event on ATTRIBUTION claims only (EV-2).

vocab_event_type.description: Facility events only (H-2), taken from MA §5.5. Other MA §5.5 types (acquired, invested, restricted and the policy types) are not instantiable in v1.

oneOf.description: The subject made public a plan or decision about a facility (a new site, an expansion or a closure), on the date the cited source gives for the announcement. A plan, never a state (ER-8): it changes no derived status.

The facility was completed or began operating, as a first-hand source states, on the date it gives. Which of the two the source says is recorded in the cited claim; neither is read as 'operating today'.
Added capacity or space at an existing facility was completed, as a first-hand source states. An expansion that is only planned is announced.
The facility stopped operating, as a first-hand source states.
